# Objectives

- use knowledge and tools encountered in BST260 to 
    - extract interesting information in public datasets of interest
    - document uncertainties and paths forward in data interpretation
- use R's pkgdown capabilities to produce GitHub pages documenting your work

# Tasks to begin

## Infrastructure, accomplish by Nov 16 2026

- fork this repository "https://github.com/vjcitn/bst260project-template" into
your account
- rename the repository to "finalproject" -- it should be a public repository
- use the github.com GitHub IDE "Settings" for the repository to enable "Pages" and use
the main branch and `/docs` folder for page management
- Change the DESCRIPTION file metadata to reflect the properties of your package
    - `Package: finalproject`
    - `Authors@R:` your identifying information
    - `URL:` and `BugReports:` fields properly set, referring to your github.com username/finalproject
    - `Depends:` and `Imports:` set properly
- Install `pkgdown` package in your R
- In the finalproject folder, run `pkgdown::build_site()`
- Visit `https://[username].github.io/finalproject` to verify that your GitHub pages site is live.
    

## Proposals, accomplish by Nov 18 2026

- Edit the document `vignettes/proposal.qmd` to state your plans regarding
the project
- Address your proposal to the "BST260 Teaching Team, Fall 2026"
- Use the requirements noted below to guide the writing of your proposal

## Requirements

- you must produce a valid R package and pkgdown site that can be seen at github.com
- you must write at least two vignettes addressing analysis tasks with *two different
datasets* encountered in the class, or approved by instructor if you are introducing new data
- you must provide 
    - full documentation of data provenance
    - descriptive statistics on the variables of interest
    - clear statement of investigative objectives
    - scientific report of findings and limitations

## Example datasets

- The NHANES or NHANESraw data from the NHANES package
- The CDC data on waterborne illnesses discussed in class [here](https://vjcitn.github.io/2026vjc/slides/prob/20-sep23-cards-cdc.html) under "Exploring the US CDC API".  The data are accessible via 
```
data(waterborne, package="bst260project") # once package is installed
```
- The CDC data on gun homicides that we explored in problem set 3.  The data are
accessible via
```
data(cdcmurd, package="bst260project")
```
- The RAND corporation data on firearms legislation in the USA.  The data are accessible
via
```
data(gunleg, package="bst260project")
```

For ideas about project activities, see the "stubs" vignette in this package.
